newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH LEGISLATORS SEAL NEW CONSTITUTION.
newsitem.headline: POLISH LEGISLATORS SEAL NEW CONSTITUTION.

text.p: Poland's national assembly of both houses of parliament gave a final go ahead on Wednesday to a new constitution that would replace the communist-era charter eight years after the fall of the old regime.

Legislators voted 451 to 40 with six abstentions to adopt the constitution, which guarantees civil and economic liberties and keeps the state and the powerful Roman Catholic church separated, after adopting some amendments proposed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
The vote paved the way for a nationwide referendum on the constitution, likley to take place in May. If approved in the poll, the charter would take effect by the end of the year.

The constitution, heatedly debated by two parliaments since 1992, has become a battleground before general elections, due around September this year. It has split the ruling leftist coalition dominated by ex-communists and non-parliamentary right-wing groups over the secular tone of the charter.

The constitution includes social security provisions, such as guarantees of free publicly funded basic health care and free basic education for all Poles. It obliges the government to work to curb unemployment and stimulate housing construction.

The presidency would be slightly weakened, with parliament allowed to overthrow the president's veto by three-fifths of votes in the lower house rather than the present two-thirds majority. The president would also have less say on appointment in the foreign, defense and interior ministries. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
